subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: measures what is where, and how much of it exists.
parts: GPS and RFID tags on freight

subsystems.name: Data integration and digital twin
subsystems.role: turns messy, multi-company data into one consistent live model of the network.
parts: entity resolution for items and suppliers
graph or relational model of the supply network

subsystems.name: Forecasting models
subsystems.role: predict demand, lead times and supply disruptions.

subsystems.name: Optimization engine
subsystems.role: chooses the allocation that best meets the stated objective under constraints.

subsystems.name: Actuation layer
subsystems.role: converts the plan into real actions.
parts: grid setpoints and battery charge commands

subsystems.name: Oversight and constraints
subsystems.role: keeps the system inside legal, safety, environmental and fairness limits.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the system
buildSteps.detail: Install meters, sensors and tags across production, transport and consumption so the state of the network is observable in near-real time.

buildSteps.title: Connect and standardise the data
buildSteps.detail: Agree common formats and identifiers so parties that do not trust each other can still exchange usable data.

buildSteps.title: Build the digital twin
buildSteps.detail: Assemble a live model of stocks, flows, capacities, lead times and prices as a single computable network.

buildSteps.title: Forecast the future state
buildSteps.detail: Run demand, yield and disruption models over horizons from minutes (grid) to seasons (agriculture).

buildSteps.title: Define the objective and constraints
buildSteps.detail: Write down what is being maximised — cost, emissions, delivery time, welfare — and the hard limits that must not be broken.

buildSteps.title: Solve the allocation problem
buildSteps.detail: Use solvers or learned policies to compute a dispatch, routing or pricing plan for the next time window.

buildSteps.title: Actuate the plan
buildSteps.detail: Send the plan into ordering, logistics, pricing and grid-control systems, or present it to human operators.

buildSteps.title: Measure and close the loop
buildSteps.detail: Compare outcomes with predictions, retrain models and adjust constraints, then repeat at each control interval.

buildSteps.title: Audit and bound
buildSteps.detail: Keep logs, test for systematic bias or concentration of harm, and retain human authority over high-impact decisions.

prerequisites.why: allocation can only be as good as the data feeding it; remote assets must report their state regularly.
planning across millions of items or nodes within minutes needs substantial parallel computing.

prerequisites.tech: Interoperable data standards and digital twins
prerequisites.why: firms and agencies hold incompatible data, so cross-sector models are still assembled by hand.
if participants gain by misreporting, the optimiser allocates on false data — a problem auction theory addresses but does not fully solve.

prerequisites.tech: Verification and safety of learned controllers
prerequisites.why: no reliable method exists to certify that a learned policy will never cause cascading failures across a critical network.
the tile's premise assumes general reasoning agents; today's systems are narrow and require a specified objective.

pathway.milestone: domain-specific optimisation in warehouses, freight, cloud capacity and electricity balancing
pathway.unlocks: measurable savings and emissions cuts inside single companies or single grids.

pathway.milestone: regional coordination across grids, ports and rail using shared standards
pathway.unlocks: shifting load and freight between operators to cut peaks and waste.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop automated markets for several commodities at once
pathway.unlocks: faster reallocation during shortages, but with new systemic risk if several systems share one model.

the theoretical post-scarcity distribution goal — only if general intelligence, incentive design and verification are all solved, and only as a hybrid with human and market control, since central planning has well-documented information and incentive limits.
